outcome.technical: In the task's own worktree, only tools/prove-gates.py was edited (git diff --stat: 1 file, 27+/1-); ci.yml was not touched. Kept attempt 1's shard_matrix_drift re-anchor (`shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` -> `[1, 2, 3, 4]`, sv7). Added three encoding_leg_drift rows. (1) TABLE (red) row after the shard row: ci.yml `'selftests-cp1252-whole' ||` -> `'selftests-cp1252' ||` (the release arm names the per-run selection), case sv7. I chose the release arm over the suggested per-run arm because the per-run swap is not specific to this lint. Measured in-process on the clean ci.yml with the real verify.sh --list: under the per-run swap slice_drift ALSO reports ('selftests-cp1252', 'a per-run slice no job outside the release tier runs...'), so sv7 would go red even with encoding_leg_drift deleted. Under the release-arm mutation slice_drift=[] and shard_matrix_drift=[], and encoding_leg_drift=[('windows code-page leg', ...)] is the only finding. sv7 is the live parity() -> slice_verdict() claim, the path the gate itself takes. If P151.8's sv17-sv19 land with a slice_verdict case for this lint, the row's case could be revisited to that id (e.g. sv18); sv7 already goes through slice_verdict, so that is optional. (2) ALLOW row: gate-parity.py `    if not release_whole:` -> `    if True:`, case el0 (the live pair). (3) ALLOW row for the other direction: `                if "per-run" in run["tiers"]:` -> `if True:`, case el3 (the release-only job fixture). Anchor counts: grep -c on each anchor -> 1, 1, 1. `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --only encoding_leg_drift` -> red half 'encoding_leg_drift RED sv7, el0, el1, el2', '1 of 1 gates proven red'; allow half both rows 'RED sv7, el0, el1, el3', '2 of 2 guards proven to stay quiet on known-good input'; exit 0 (worker trees, checkout not written). el1/el2 also go red under the red mutation because their replace of the release arm becomes a no-op on already-mutated text, which is expected. `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --selftest` -> exit 0, 'ALL PASS: 65/65 cases passed' (c1, c2 and a4 now pass). `python3 tools/gate-parity.py --selftest` -> 'ALL PASS: 103/103'; `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` -> exit 0. `ruff check tools/prove-gates.py` -> 'All checks passed!', exit 0. In-process _output_lints.prose_number_claims() -> 0 findings. `tests/test__refs.py --selftest` -> 292/292. Per the brief (own-tests, no tests.add) there was no gate of my own to run, so gates is {}; the commands above are extra evidence. The full sweep was not run here; the orchestrator's recorded run is the verdict. Dependants: the eight path-dependants of prove-gates.py (.github/sweep-costs.json, guard-bash-writes.py, tests/_harness.py, test__deps.py, test__gate_feed.py, test_drive_phase.py, test_guard_bash_writes.py, tools/affected.py) refer to its path, which did not change, so they are still correct. The names used elsewhere (_under, selector_text, _call_name, changed_paths) were not touched, so they are still correct.
